A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Mantis, despite substantial revisions to its architecture, training and evaluation. Text, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable and support a reliable comparison, including v1 Appendices A–B and v2 Appendices A–D.

before.justification: v1 reports original classification, fine-tuning, architecture-ablation, adapter, runtime and calibration experiments in Section 3 and Appendix B.

after.justification: v2 reports original benchmark evaluations, domain-shift experiments, runtime measurements and extensive ablations in Section 4 and Appendices B–D. These include original outcomes beyond the published baseline results it also reproduces.

M1.justification: The multibranch tokenizer and contrastive objective remain, but v2 adopts RoPE, RMSNorm and SwiGLU and introduces intermediate-layer extraction, classification-token/mean-token concatenation, multiple-interpolation self-ensembling and cross-model embedding fusion (Sections 3.2–3.4 and Appendix B). These change the architecture and inference procedure. PCA and the earlier LComb adapter remain as PCA and Linear in Appendix C.2.

E1.justification: v1 pre-trains on seven million real time series; v2 uses CauKer synthetic data for its main model, retaining real-data pre-training as an ablation. UCR and UEA coverage remains, while Ego4D, HHAR, Military Press, CAP and PCL substantially expand evaluation, including held-out device, source and age scenarios. MotionSenseHAR and SharePriceIncrease disappear; Blink and EMOPain are retained within the new domain collections.

E2.justification: Beyond retained NuTime and MOMENT, v2 evaluates Catch22+, TabPFN, TabICL, TiRex, Chronos2, TiViT-H and TiConvNext, and includes published self-supervised and supervised comparisons on UCR-91 (Figure 1 and Table 17). UniTS and GPT4TS are no longer evaluated. Adapter comparisons retain PCA and Linear/LComb but remove SVD, random projection and variance-based selection.

E3.justification: v2 introduces a UCR-91 comparison using standardized features and logistic regression, while retaining 200-tree Random Forests for the broader benchmark breakdown. Its Mantis fine-tuning study uses 500 epochs, batch size 128 and a fixed learning rate, replacing v1's 100-epoch, batch-256 studies and their model-selection comparisons. New domain-held-out protocols and synthetic sample-size runtime experiments also change the evaluation design.

E4.justification: v2 expands the differential-branch ablation into tokenizer capacity controls, pooling/kernel/backbone comparisons, real-versus-synthetic pre-training, matched-update layer analyses, token aggregation, self-ensembling, loss, augmentation and predictor-normalization studies. It adds TabPFN subgroup analyses and domain-shift tests. Earlier scratch/head/full comparisons are replaced by different fine-tuning analyses; adapter analysis is narrowed, and calibration/reliability studies are removed.

E5.justification: v1 explicitly identifies benchmark results as averages over three seeds with standard deviations. v2 retains many ± entries but drops these explanations from the corresponding benchmark-table captions; three-seed/run statements remain for particular architecture and fine-tuning experiments. Its adapter Table 12 reports point estimates without v1 Table 2's uncertainty. There is no documented increase in runs or new significance-testing procedure.

E6.justification: Results are extensively replaced and supplemented. v1 Figure 3 reports 0.7816 accuracy over 159 datasets; v2 Table 1 reports 0.8195 on full UCR and 0.7420 on UEA-27, alongside new HAR/EEG, layer-selection, ensemble and fusion results. v1's calibration results, including uncalibrated Mantis ECE 0.1131, disappear. Changed models, dataset groupings and protocols prevent treating these aggregate differences as same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: v2 Appendix B.5 adds a short mathematical calculation relating interpolation length to token receptive field, including its limiting fraction of 1/32. v1's formal confidence and calibration definitions disappear with the calibration study. The core contrastive formulation remains equivalent, and neither version develops a substantial theorem-and-proof framework.

C1.justification: v1 foregrounds superiority in frozen and fine-tuned classification, best calibration and resource-saving multivariate adapters. v2 reframes the contributions around synthetic pre-training, tokenization and enhanced frozen-encoder inference, claiming competitiveness with strong dataset-specific methods as well as other foundation models. Calibration superiority and adapter development are no longer headline contributions.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations linking intermediate-layer advantages to contrastive-objective overfitting, data scaling and complementary token information. It discusses normalization-dependent probing, cross-model complementarity and TabPFN's dataset-dependent strengths. New qualifications include self-ensembling not improving UCR-91 and reconstruction objectives potentially requiring another architecture. Earlier calibration interpretations and detailed adapter failure discussions are removed or substantially reduced.

D1.justification: v2 adds dataset characteristics, domain-split rules, preprocessing references, baseline package versions/checkpoint references, probing settings and explicit self-ensemble interpolation lengths. It also documents revised fine-tuning settings. Conversely, v1's explicit pre-training batch size of 2048, four-V100 hardware specification and evaluation hardware disclosure are absent. The main source-code link remains the same.

R1.justification: v2 adds a dedicated Related Work section and substantially expands positioning around synthetic pre-training, forecasting/vision/tabular foundation models and intermediate representations, including CauKer, TiRex, Chronos2, Roschmann et al. and Skean et al. Adapters are now presented as following Benechehab et al. and Ilbert et al., rather than as a headline contribution. Much calibration-related literature is removed.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, experimental narrative and conclusion are extensively rewritten around frozen-encoder inference. Related Work becomes a separate section, preprocessing is integrated into the architecture description, and fine-tuning/adapters move into a reorganized appendix. Terminology is clarified, including the meaning of zero-shot feature extraction. These are substantial narrative and structural changes beyond renumbering.

P2.justification: The single-column technical report becomes a two-column conference paper. The architecture diagram is revised, calibration and earlier fine-tuning displays disappear, and new layer-by-epoch, token-aggregation, scaling and ensemble figures are introduced. Benchmark tables are redesigned around method families and domain collections, with substantially different appendix table structures.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens the empirical basis for its design and generalization claims. Table 7 compares real and synthetic pre-training; Appendix B controls tokenizer capacity and separates training-update effects from data scale; Table 2 adds held-out-domain evaluations. These address important gaps in v1's architectural controls and transfer evidence, while broader baseline families strengthen comparisons. Calibration and broad cross-model fine-tuning evidence are lost, and some reproducibility and uncertainty reporting deteriorates. Nevertheless, the controlled analyses and stronger support for the refocused claims provide a substantial net quality improvement.
